title: September-quarter results are due next
text: The next quarterly report is scheduled for 29 October, with a 10am Sydney briefing. June 2026 remains the latest available quarter in this site’s 28 October snapshot.

title: Annual meeting set for 25 November
text: The amended shareholder letter sets the AGM for 25 November 2026 at 10am AEDT, in Sydney and online.

title: Meteoric proposal would add Brazilian feedstock
text: An all-scrip scheme proposes 0.0207 new Lynas shares per Meteoric share. The A$968m implied fully diluted equity value uses Lynas’ 60-day VWAP. Shareholder, court and regulatory conditions remain; implementation is expected by March 2027. Caldeira is not an operating Lynas asset.

title: FY26 revenue reaches A$977.9m
text: Revenue rose 75.7% from FY25. Cash and term deposits reached A$1,209.1m, supported by an equity raising as well as operational performance. Cash growth should not be read as operating cash flow alone.

title: LS Eco Energy cross investment
text: Binding agreements cover approximately A$29m of convertible instruments each: zero interest, five-year maturity and holder conversion after three years. Conditions apply. A definitive Vietnam metal-processing agreement was still being negotiated.

title: Heavy rare earth expansion cost estimate rises
text: The June-quarter report updates estimated HRE expansion capex from A$180m to A$294m including contingency. It targets gadolinium in early FY28 and yttrium in early calendar 2028. These are planned milestones.

title: JS Link plans a Malaysian magnet factory
text: The agreement supports a planned 3,000tpa NdFeB magnet factory in Kuantan. Lynas invested approximately A$50m in JS Link equity and agreed exclusive rare-earth supply to Yesan and the planned Malaysian factory through January 2038.

title: Updated EIA requested for Malaysia
text: Malaysia’s Department of Environment requested an updated environmental impact assessment following technical review. The release said Lynas would resubmit. The operating licence and expansion approvals are separate issues.

title: First samarium oxide produced
text: Lynas reported first Sm oxide production in Malaysia, extending its separated heavy rare earth product range. First production does not establish the timing or volume of commercial shipments.

title: JARE agreement adds a price floor
text: Firm NdPr offtake is 5,000tpa with a US$110/kg floor. Above US$150/kg, 30% upside sharing is capped at US$10m per calendar year. Review provisions apply. This is not a floor on the entire REO sales basket.

title: Malaysia licence renewed for a decade
text: The company reported a ten-year operating licence renewal commencing 3 March 2026. This provides operating tenure while separate approvals still matter for expansion projects.
